exposure: Oxytocin (10 IU IV in 500 mL normal saline)
cohort: 200 pregnant women at high risk for postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) undergoing cesarean section.
finding: Carbetocin significantly reduced intraoperative blood loss, improved uterine tone, decreased the need for additional uterotonics, resulted in less postoperative hemoglobin fall, and maintained better hemodynamic stability compared to oxytocin in high-risk cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: Carbetocin was found to be more effective than oxytocin in managing high-risk cesarean deliveries for PPH prevention.
